sentences.text: Marasuchus is an early genus of dinosauriform archosaur and a close relative of dinosaurs.
This animal possessed long, slender limbs where the hindlimbs were about twice the length of the forelimbs, while the entire forelimb was only about half the size of the hindlimb.
It featured a relatively long neck with an S-shaped curve and a very long, thin tail that was deeper at the base.
Although several specimens show most of the skeleton, skull material is limited and the hand is entirely unknown.
The braincase was tall and typical for early archosaurs but shared some similarities with early dinosaur braincases.
Most of the unique traits that define Marasuchus are found in its vertebrae.
Its neck was long and curved, created by elongated neck vertebrae with offset ends, similar to other bird-lineage archosaurs.
The upper blade of the hip, the ilium, was similar in general shape to that of Herrerasaurus.
A ridge of bone called the trochanteric shelf branched from the anterior trochanter and wrapped around the femur shaft.
Marasuchus was a small predator only 40 centimeters long.
It is one of the most completely known avemetatarsalians, providing key insights into the early evolution of dinosaur-like traits.
The species Marasuchus lilloensis was originally named Lagosuchus lilloensis in 1972.
Marasuchus fossils were named after specimens stored at the PVL museum in San Miguel de Tucuman.
The first known remains of Marasuchus were found during a 1964-1965 paleontological expedition.
Alfred Romer described the fossils found during the expedition in a series of papers.
The holotype specimen PVL 3871 was collected by Jose Bonaparte in 1969.
The type species of the genus Marasuchus is Marasuchus illoensis.
The species Marasuchus illoensis was described by Sereno and Arcucci in 1994.
Lagosuchus lilloensis, described by Romer in 1972, is a synonym of Marasuchus.
The species Marasuchus lilloensis was originally described as a second species of Lagosuchus, named L. lilloensis.
In a 1994 restudy, Sereno and Arcucci concluded that the original Lagosuchus type specimen was too poorly preserved to allow adding additional specimens to that genus.
Sereno and Arcucci noted that the L. lilloensis specimen had different limb proportions compared to the type species.
Its body proportions suggest Marasuchus was probably bipedal, walking on its hindlimbs.
In 1994, Sereno and Arcucci created the genus Marasuchus for better-preserved fossils because they considered Lagosuchus talampayensis a nomen dubium.
Marasuchus belonged to Avemetatarsalia, the archosaur branch closer to birds and dinosaurs than to crocodilians.
It was classified as a dinosauriform, placing it closer to dinosaurs than to lagerpetids.
While not as closely related to dinosaurs as silesaurids like Silesaurus, Marasuchus is one of the most completely known avemetatarsalians and helps understand early dinosaur-like evolution.
Marasuchus lived in the Late Triassic (early Carnian stage) in what is now La Rioja Province, Argentina.
Marasuchus fossils come from the Chañares Formation, dated to 235 to 234 million years ago.
Marasuchus was an extinct ornithodiran archosaur that lived during the Middle Triassic (Ladinian, about 230 million years ago) in the Chañares Formation in La Rioja, Argentina.
Marasuchus lived from 241.464 to 237 million years ago during the Ladinian stage.
It is debated whether Marasuchus is a valid genus or a junior synonym of Lagosuchus.
A 2019 study suggested that Marasuchus lilloensis might be a synonym of Lagosuchus talampayensis after re-examining the type specimen.
A 2024 study concluded that Marasuchus and Lagosuchus represent the same animal, with Lagosuchus talampayensis having priority.
